prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t pick one single lawyer for you, but I can help you choose the right lawyer and give you practical next steps to find a good Pleasanton / Alameda County personal injury attorney. If you want, I can also pull a short list of local firms that match your needs — tell me a few details (date of crash, severity of injury, insurance situation) and I’ll do that.

What to look for in a personal-injury lawyer
- Relevant experience: handled car-accident cases, ideally with experience in Alameda County courts and with your type/severity of injury.
- Trial and settlement experience: some cases settle quickly; others require suit and trial. Ask about verdicts and appellate experience.
- Resources: ability to fund medical records collection, expert witnesses, accident reconstruction, and litigation costs.
- Communication: clear point of contact, timely responses, and whether they or an assistant will handle most of your questions.
- Reputation and discipline history: good reviews, peer ratings, and a clean California State Bar record.

Where to search and how to check credentials
- California State Bar Lawyer Search (search bar number and disciplinary history).
- Local bar associations (Alameda County Bar Association) referral lists.
- Legal directories: Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers — read reviews and peer ratings.
- Google and Yelp reviews — take single reviews with caution; look at patterns.
- Ask friends, family, or other attorneys you trust for referrals.

Questions to ask at the free consultation
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled? What were the outcomes?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?
- What is your fee structure? Typical contingency percentage? Any additional costs I’d be responsible for?
- What’s your estimate of my case’s value and likely timeline?
- Have you taken cases to trial? How often do you settle vs. go to trial?
- Can you provide references from recent clients (or examples of verdicts/settlements)?
- How will we communicate (email, phone, text) and how quickly can I expect responses?

Typical fees and billing (what to expect)
- Most personal injury lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover).
- Contingency fees commonly range about 33%–40% of the recovery; it can be higher if suit or appeals are required. Always confirm the exact percentage and how costs are handled.
- You may be responsible for case costs (expert fees, medical record retrieval, filing fees) if the case is lost — confirm the retainer agreement details.

Immediate practical steps you should take now
- Seek and continue medical treatment; follow providers’ instructions and keep records.
- Preserve evidence: photos, videos, the police report number, witness names and contact info, damaged vehicle info.
- Do not give recorded statements to the other party’s insurer without consulting a lawyer.
- Notify your insurer as required, but be careful with descriptions; confirm with an attorney if possible.
- Keep a diary of symptoms, doctor visits, missed work, and expenses.

Time-sensitivity (important)
- California’s general statute of limitations for personal injury is usually 2 years from the date of the injury. If a government entity is involved, special shorter notice requirements apply. Don’t delay in talking to an attorney.

Red flags in a lawyer
- Vague answers about experience or fees.
- No written agreement.
- Promises of a specific dollar amount before reviewing records.
- Poor communication or lack of willingness to put things in writing.

If you want, I can:
- Find and list 3–6 Pleasanton or Alameda County personal injury firms with good ratings and relevant experience.
- Draft a short script of what to say in your initial call or a checklist to bring to consultations.

If you want that shortlist, tell me:
- Date of accident
- Your injuries / whether you’ve been treated
- Whether the other driver was clearly at fault / insurance info
- Any urgent deadlines you’re worried about

Would you like me to find local attorneys now?
